authors: Peter Cotton
title: An Analytic Approach to Ornstein-Uhlenbeck Processes with Fluctuating Parameters and Applications in the Modeling of Fixed Income Securities
annotation: Treats Ornstein-Uhlenbeck short rates and hazard rates whose parameters are driven by a Markov chain. It reduces bond prices and survival probabilities to a linear system of ordinary differential equations and expands them for fast switching. Its second half is developed to all orders in the regime-switching pages.

authors: Alain Bensoussan, Jacques-Louis Lions, George Papanicolaou
title: Asymptotic Analysis for Periodic Structures
venue: North-Holland, Studies in Mathematics and its Applications 5 (reprinted AMS Chelsea Publishing, 2011)
annotation: The standard reference for two-scale expansions and correctors in elliptic and parabolic equations with rapidly varying coefficients, including the probabilistic treatment of diffusions in periodic and random media on which the corrector calculation is modelled; the DOI is for the 2011 AMS Chelsea reprint.

authors: George C. Papanicolaou, Daniel W. Stroock, S. R. Srinivasa Varadhan
title: Martingale approach to some limit theorems
venue: Papers from the Duke Turbulence Conference (Durham, NC, 1976), Duke University Mathematics Series III, Duke University
annotation: Proves diffusion limits for processes driven by fast ergodic Markov noise via the martingale problem, supplying the Poisson-equation and perturbed test function arguments that justify replacing the fast regime by its average.

authors: R. Z. Khas'minskii
title: A Limit Theorem for the Solutions of Differential Equations with Random Right-Hand Sides
venue: Theory of Probability and Its Applications 11(3):390-406
annotation: Establishes the averaging and diffusion-approximation limit for differential equations driven by rapidly mixing random coefficients, the prototype for letting the regime chain switch at rate 1/epsilon.

authors: Thomas G. Kurtz
title: A limit theorem for perturbed operator semigroups with applications to random evolutions
annotation: Gives an operator-semigroup limit theorem for singularly perturbed generators of the form (1/epsilon)Q + L, which covers random evolutions such as an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process modulated by a fast Markov chain.

authors: Grigorios A. Pavliotis, Andrew M. Stuart
title: Multiscale Methods: Averaging and Homogenization
annotation: A textbook treatment of formal multiscale expansions for Markov chains, ODEs, SDEs and PDEs, including a chapter on averaging for Markov chains that matches the two-state switching setting.

authors: M. I. Freidlin, A. D. Wentzell
title: Random Perturbations of Dynamical Systems
annotation: Develops the averaging principle and associated large deviations for systems with fast and slow components, which describe the leading-order behaviour and rare-event corrections beyond a power-series expansion in epsilon.

authors: G. George Yin, Qing Zhang
title: Continuous-Time Markov Chains and Applications: A Singular Perturbation Approach
venue: Springer, Applications of Mathematics 37 (2nd ed. 2013, doi 10.1007/978-1-4614-4346-9)
annotation: Constructs asymptotic expansions, with outer and initial-layer terms, for probability distributions of Markov chains with generators of the form Q/epsilon, the general machinery behind expanding in the inverse switching rate.

authors: R. Z. Khasminskii, G. Yin
title: Asymptotic Series for Singularly Perturbed Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck Equations
annotation: Derives full asymptotic series with error bounds for Kolmogorov-Fokker-Planck equations of diffusions with fast and slow components.

authors: A. M. Il'in, R. Z. Khasminskii, G. Yin
title: Asymptotic Expansions of Solutions of Integro-Differential Equations for Transition Densities of Singularly Perturbed Switching Diffusions: Rapid Switchings
venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 238(2):516-539
annotation: Obtains asymptotic expansions of the transition densities of diffusions whose coefficients are modulated by a rapidly switching Markov chain, the density-level analogue of the expansion for a Markov-modulated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process.

authors: Gang Huang, Michel Mandjes, Peter Spreij
title: Weak convergence of Markov-modulated diffusion processes with rapid switching
annotation: Proves that a diffusion whose drift and diffusion coefficients are modulated by a rapidly switching Markov chain converges weakly to the diffusion with averaged coefficients, which is the leading-order statement underlying the averaged Vasicek limit.

authors: Gang Huang, H. M. Jansen, Michel Mandjes, Peter Spreij, Koen De Turck
title: Markov-modulated Ornstein-Uhlenbeck processes
annotation: Computes moments and Laplace-transform PDEs of an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process with Markov-modulated parameters and proves functional central limit theorems when the modulating chain is accelerated, which is the regime-switching state process studied as a process rather than through its exponential functional.

authors: Gang Huang, Michel Mandjes, Peter Spreij
title: Large deviations for Markov-modulated diffusion processes with rapid switching
annotation: Proves a joint sample-path large deviations principle for a Markov-modulated diffusion and the chain's occupation measure under rapid switching and small noise.

authors: Jean-Pierre Fouque, George Papanicolaou, K. Ronnie Sircar
title: Derivatives in Financial Markets with Stochastic Volatility
annotation: Introduces fast mean-reverting stochastic volatility asymptotics in which prices are expanded around an effective constant-volatility model with a first-order correction, the template for the fast regime chain.

authors: Jean-Pierre Fouque, George Papanicolaou, Ronnie Sircar, Knut Sølna
title: Multiscale Stochastic Volatility for Equity, Interest Rate, and Credit Derivatives
annotation: Extends the fast and slow scale expansions to interest rate and credit models, including Vasicek and CIR bond prices and defaultable bonds with stochastic intensity. It is the closest book-length treatment of the regime-switching problem, with a diffusive fast factor instead of a Markov chain.

authors: Peter Cotton, Jean-Pierre Fouque, George Papanicolaou, Ronnie Sircar
title: Stochastic Volatility Corrections for Interest Rate Derivatives
annotation: Derives the corrections to Vasicek and CIR bond prices when the volatility of the short rate is driven by a fast mean-reverting factor. The regime-switching expansion is the same calculation with a two-state chain in place of the diffusion.

authors: Jean-Pierre Fouque, George Papanicolaou, Ronnie Sircar, Knut Sølna
title: Multiscale Stochastic Volatility Asymptotics
annotation: Combines a fast and a slow volatility factor in a joint singular and regular perturbation expansion of option prices.

authors: Jean-Pierre Fouque, George Papanicolaou, Ronnie Sircar, Knut Sølna
title: Singular Perturbations in Option Pricing
annotation: Gives the error analysis that justifies the first-order fast-scale correction for option prices, including nonsmooth payoffs.

authors: Rafael DeSantiago, Jean-Pierre Fouque, Knut Sølna
title: Bond markets with stochastic volatility
venue: Advances in Econometrics 22 (Econometrics and Risk Management):215-242
annotation: Computes fast and slow stochastic volatility corrections to Vasicek and CIR bond prices, again with a diffusive volatility factor where the regime-switching example uses a two-state chain.

authors: Oldrich Vasicek
title: An equilibrium characterization of the term structure
annotation: Introduces the Ornstein-Uhlenbeck short rate and its exponential-affine bond price, which is the model obtained in each regime and in the averaged limit.

authors: John C. Cox, Jonathan E. Ingersoll Jr., Stephen A. Ross
title: A Theory of the Term Structure of Interest Rates
annotation: Introduces the square-root short rate model with exponential-affine bond prices, the natural alternative regime dynamics when positivity of the hazard rate is required.

authors: Darrell Duffie, Rui Kan
title: A Yield-Factor Model of Interest Rates
annotation: Characterizes the multifactor affine term structure models in which bond prices are exponential-affine with coefficients solving Riccati equations.

authors: James D. Hamilton
title: A New Approach to the Economic Analysis of Nonstationary Time Series and the Business Cycle
annotation: Introduces the Markov-switching time series model and its filter, the econometric origin of regime-switching interest rate and credit models.

authors: Camilla Landén
title: Bond pricing in a hidden Markov model of the short rate
annotation: Studies a short rate whose drift and diffusion parameters are modulated by a possibly unobserved Markov process, introduces semi-affine term structures, gives a closed-form bond price when the chain has two states, and studies a Vasicek extension numerically.

authors: Asbjørn T. Hansen, Rolf Poulsen
title: A simple regime switching term structure model
annotation: Proposes a short-rate model with Markov regime switching in the parameters and studies its term structure, appearing in the same issue as Landén (2000).

authors: Robert J. Elliott, Rogemar S. Mamon
title: An interest rate model with a Markovian mean reverting level
annotation: Takes a Vasicek short rate whose mean-reversion level is driven by a finite-state Markov chain and gives the bond price analytically through a fundamental matrix. It covers the regime-switching Vasicek model in the case of equal volatilities.

authors: Andrew Ang, Geert Bekaert
title: Regime Switches in Interest Rates
venue: Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 20(2):163-182
annotation: Estimates regime-switching short-rate models on US, UK and German data and documents that regimes capture nonlinearities in drift and volatility.

authors: Ravi Bansal, Hao Zhou
title: Term Structure of Interest Rates with Regime Shifts
annotation: Builds a discrete-time affine term structure model with regime shifts using log-linear approximations and finds that regime shifts improve the fit to yields.

authors: Shu Wu, Yong Zeng
title: A General Equilibrium Model of the Term Structure of Interest Rates under Regime-Switching Risk
venue: International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance 8(7):839-869
annotation: Develops an equilibrium term structure model with priced regime-shift risk and obtains closed-form affine yields under a log-linear approximation.

authors: Robert J. Elliott, Tak Kuen Siu
title: On Markov-modulated Exponential-affine Bond Price Formulae
annotation: Proves Markov-modulated exponential-affine bond price formulae for regime-switching Hull-White and CIR short rates, with coefficients given by fundamental matrix solutions of linear matrix differential equations, which contains the reduction used in the examples as a special case.

authors: Misha van Beek, Michel Mandjes, Peter Spreij, Erik Winands
title: Regime switching affine processes with applications to finance
annotation: Shows that an affine process with Markov-switching parameters is affine on the enlarged state space, so transforms reduce to ODE systems, unifying earlier semi-analytic regime-switching bond formulas.

authors: Marianito R. Rodrigo, Rogemar S. Mamon
title: Bond pricing formulas for Markov-modulated affine term structure models
venue: Journal of Industrial and Management Optimization 17(5):2685ff
annotation: Gives exact and approximate zero-coupon bond formulas for Markov-modulated affine short rates with time-dependent coefficients and validates them on a regime-switching Vasicek model.

authors: G. Yin
title: Asymptotic expansions of option price under regime-switching diffusions with a fast-varying switching process
annotation: Develops uniform asymptotic expansions, with averaged Black-Scholes leading term and full series, for European option prices when the regime chain switches fast, the closest published analogue of the regime-switching expansion but for equity options rather than bond prices.

authors: David D. Yao, Qing Zhang, Xun Yu Zhou
title: A Regime-Switching Model for European Options
venue: in Stochastic Processes, Optimization, and Control Theory (H. Yan, G. Yin, Q. Zhang, eds.), Springer, International Series in Operations Research and Management Science, pp. 281-300
annotation: Prices European options in a Black-Scholes model with Markov-switching parameters by successive approximation of the coupled pricing system.

authors: Arnab Basu, Mrinal K. Ghosh
title: Asymptotic analysis of option pricing in a Markov modulated market
annotation: Analyzes Markov-modulated option prices in the limits where the chain moves very fast or very slowly relative to the asset.

authors: Andrew Papanicolaou, Ronnie Sircar
title: A regime-switching Heston model for VIX and S&P 500 implied volatilities
annotation: Adds Markov regime switching to Heston stochastic volatility to fit VIX and S&P 500 option smiles jointly, an equity counterpart of combining a regime chain with an affine factor.

authors: David Lando
title: On Cox Processes and Credit Risky Securities
annotation: Models default as the first jump of a Cox process so that survival probabilities take the form E[exp(-integral of the intensity)], the quantity computed for a regime-switching intensity.

authors: Darrell Duffie, Kenneth J. Singleton
title: Modeling Term Structures of Defaultable Bonds
annotation: Shows that defaultable bonds can be priced by discounting at a default-adjusted short rate, so survival probabilities and bond prices are the same computation.

authors: Darrell Duffie, Jun Pan, Kenneth Singleton
title: Transform Analysis and Asset Pricing for Affine Jump-Diffusions
annotation: Gives the general exponential-affine transform formula for affine jump-diffusions via Riccati ODEs, the framework within which regime switching is accommodated by enlarging the state space.

authors: R. Duncan Luce
title: Individual Choice Behavior: A Theoretical Analysis
annotation: Axiomatizes probabilistic choice through the choice axiom, yielding the ratio-scale choice model used elsewhere in the author's program.

authors: Vladimir Vovk, Alex Gammerman, Glenn Shafer
title: Algorithmic Learning in a Random World
annotation: Develops conformal prediction, giving distribution-free prediction sets with guaranteed coverage under exchangeability.

authors: Steven L. Heston
title: A Closed-Form Solution for Options with Stochastic Volatility with Applications to Bond and Currency Options
annotation: Introduces the square-root stochastic variance model and its characteristic function; the Heston example lets the long-run variance switch.

authors: Alan L. Lewis
title: A Simple Option Formula for General Jump-Diffusion and Other Exponential Levy Processes
annotation: Gives the single-integral option price in terms of the characteristic function that the Heston example uses.

authors: Wolfgang Fischer, Kathleen Meier-Hellstern
title: The Markov-modulated Poisson process (MMPP) cookbook
annotation: Collects the generating functions, moments and fitting methods of the Markov-modulated Poisson process, the model in the Poisson counts example.

authors: Kubo, R.
title: Generalized Cumulant Expansion Method
venue: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 17(7):1100-1120
annotation: Generalizes cumulant expansions to non-commuting operators with ordered exponentials, the tool behind stochastic line-shape and relaxation theory.

authors: Griego, R. J. and Hersh, R.
title: Random Evolutions, Markov Chains, and Systems of Partial Differential Equations
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 62(2):305-308
annotation: Introduces random evolutions: operators switched by a Markov chain, whose expectations solve coupled systems of partial differential equations. This is the structure of every pricing equation in the examples.

authors: Papanicolaou, G. C. and Varadhan, S. R. S.
title: A limit theorem with strong mixing in Banach space and two applications to stochastic differential equations
venue: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 26(4):497-524
annotation: A limit theorem for evolutions driven by strongly mixing noise in a Banach space, applied to stochastic differential equations; an early operator form of the diffusion approximation.

authors: Papanicolaou, G. C. and Kohler, W.
title: Asymptotic theory of mixing stochastic ordinary differential equations
venue: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 27(5):641-668
annotation: The asymptotic theory of ordinary differential equations with fast mixing random coefficients, in which the limit is a diffusion whose coefficients are integrated correlation functions.

authors: Hersh, R.
title: Random evolutions: A survey of results and problems
annotation: A survey of random evolutions and their limit theorems under rescaling.

authors: van Kampen, N. G.
title: A cumulant expansion for stochastic linear differential equations. I
annotation: A cumulant expansion for linear differential equations with random coefficients. Its second-order term is the time-ordered, correlation-weighted product of the random operators, the physicists' form of the first-order rule for switched operators.

authors: Phillips, R. G. and Kokotovic, P. V.
title: A singular perturbation approach to modeling and control of Markov chains
annotation: Singular perturbation for Markov chains with weak and strong interactions, the control-theory origin of aggregating fast states.

authors: Ethier, S. N. and Kurtz, T. G.
title: Markov Processes: Characterization and Convergence
annotation: The standard reference for convergence of Markov processes through generators and martingale problems, with a chapter on random evolutions and diffusion approximations.

authors: Pinsky, M. A.
title: Lectures on Random Evolution
annotation: Lectures on random evolutions, including their averaging and diffusion-approximation limits.

authors: Pardoux, E. and Veretennikov, A. Yu.
title: On the Poisson Equation and Diffusion Approximation. I
annotation: Solves the Poisson equation for the generator of an ergodic diffusion on the whole space and uses it to prove diffusion approximations; the continuous-state version of solving Q w = f.

authors: Skorokhod, A. V., Hoppensteadt, F. C. and Salehi, H.
title: Random Perturbation Methods with Applications in Science and Engineering
annotation: Averaging and diffusion approximation for systems perturbed by fast random processes, with applications across science and engineering.

authors: Kushner, H. J. and Yin, G. G.
title: Stochastic Approximation and Recursive Algorithms and Applications
venue: Springer, Stochastic Modelling and Applied Probability 35, 2nd ed.
annotation: Stochastic approximation with correlated and Markovian noise, where the averaged ordinary differential equation and the fluctuation limit play the roles of the averaged law and the Green-Kubo correction.

authors: Fouque, J.-P., Garnier, J., Papanicolaou, G. and Sølna, K.
title: Wave Propagation and Time Reversal in Randomly Layered Media
venue: Springer, Stochastic Modelling and Applied Probability 56
annotation: Waves in randomly layered media treated by the diffusion approximation for fast random coefficients, including the effective medium and the first corrections.

authors: Yin, G. G. and Zhang, Q.
title: Continuous-Time Markov Chains and Applications: A Two-Time-Scale Approach
venue: Springer, Stochastic Modelling and Applied Probability 37, 2nd ed.
annotation: The second edition of the two-time-scale Markov chain monograph, with outer expansions, initial layers and applications to control and finance.

authors: Hull, J. and White, A.
title: The Pricing of Options on Assets with Stochastic Volatilities
annotation: Prices an option under uncorrelated stochastic volatility as the Black-Scholes price averaged over integrated variance. Its expansion to second order in the variance of integrated variance is the smile formula on the any-equation page.

authors: Naik, V.
title: Option Valuation and Hedging Strategies with Jumps in the Volatility of Asset Returns
annotation: Option valuation when volatility jumps between two levels following a Markov chain, one of the first regime-switching option pricing models.

authors: Di Masi, G. B., Kabanov, Yu. M. and Runggaldier, W. J.
title: Mean-Variance Hedging of Options on Stocks with Markov Volatilities
venue: Theory of Probability and Its Applications 39(1):172-182
annotation: Mean-variance hedging of options on a stock whose volatility is driven by a Markov chain.

authors: Sircar, K. R. and Papanicolaou, G. C.
title: Stochastic volatility, smile & asymptotics
annotation: Stochastic volatility, the smile and asymptotics: an early account of how fast volatility fluctuations produce a smile around an effective constant volatility.

authors: Fouque, J.-P., Papanicolaou, G. and Sircar, K. R.
title: Mean-Reverting Stochastic Volatility
venue: International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance 3(1):101-142
annotation: The paper that introduced fast mean-reverting stochastic volatility asymptotics for option pricing, with the first correction expressed through a few group parameters that can be fitted to the implied volatility skew.

authors: Guo, X.
title: Information and option pricings
annotation: Option pricing with a two-state regime-switching volatility and the role of information about the regime.

authors: Buffington, J. and Elliott, R. J.
title: American Options with Regime Switching
venue: International Journal of Theoretical and Applied Finance 5(5):497-514
annotation: European and American options when the parameters of the underlying switch with a Markov chain.

authors: Elliott, R. J., Chan, L. and Siu, T. K.
title: Option pricing and Esscher transform under regime switching
annotation: Regime-switching option pricing with the equivalent martingale measure chosen by the Esscher transform.

authors: Fouque, J.-P., Sircar, R. and Sølna, K.
title: Stochastic Volatility Effects on Defaultable Bonds
annotation: Fast and slow stochastic volatility corrections for defaultable bonds and credit spreads.

authors: Fouque, J.-P., Wignall, B. C. and Zhou, X.
title: Modeling correlated defaults: first passage model under stochastic volatility
annotation: Correlated defaults in a first-passage model under stochastic volatility, with the joint default probabilities corrected by multiscale asymptotics.

authors: Duffie, D., Eckner, A., Horel, G. and Saita, L.
title: Frailty Correlated Default
annotation: Evidence that US corporate defaults cluster beyond what observable covariates explain, modelled with a common latent frailty process driving all default intensities.

authors: Fouque, J.-P., Lorig, M. and Sircar, R.
title: Second order multiscale stochastic volatility asymptotics: stochastic terminal layer analysis and calibration
annotation: Second-order multiscale stochastic volatility asymptotics, including a stochastic terminal layer, with calibration to implied volatilities.

authors: Fouque, J.-P., Sircar, R. and Zariphopoulou, T.
title: Portfolio Optimization and Stochastic Volatility Asymptotics
annotation: Applies fast and slow volatility asymptotics to Merton's portfolio problem, showing the first correction to the value function and the optimal strategy.

authors: Onsager, L.
title: Reciprocal Relations in Irreversible Processes. I.
annotation: The reciprocal relations: transport coefficients are symmetric under microscopic reversibility. The same argument makes the Green-Kubo matrix symmetric for a reversible chain.

authors: Bloembergen, N., Purcell, E. M. and Pound, R. V.
title: Relaxation Effects in Nuclear Magnetic Resonance Absorption
annotation: Nuclear magnetic relaxation in liquids, with relaxation rates set by spectral densities of fluctuating local fields.

authors: Taylor, G. I.
title: Dispersion of soluble matter in solvent flowing slowly through a tube
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 219(1137):186-203
annotation: Dispersion of a solute in flow through a tube: shear and cross-stream diffusion combine into an enhanced effective diffusion along the tube.

authors: Green, M. S.
title: Markoff Random Processes and the Statistical Mechanics of Time-Dependent Phenomena. II. Irreversible Processes in Fluids
annotation: Expresses transport coefficients in fluids as time integrals of equilibrium correlation functions, one half of the Green-Kubo formula.

authors: Anderson, P. W.
title: A Mathematical Model for the Narrowing of Spectral Lines by Exchange or Motion
venue: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 9(3):316-339
annotation: Exchange narrowing of spectral lines: a frequency that hops between values produces a line whose width falls as the hopping speeds up. The two-site case is the two-state eigenvalue on the yield-curve page with an imaginary forcing.

authors: Kubo, R.
title: Note on the Stochastic Theory of Resonance Absorption
venue: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 9(6):935-944
annotation: The stochastic theory of resonance absorption and motional narrowing, with the line width given by the integrated correlation of the frequency fluctuation.

authors: Giddings, J. C. and Eyring, H.
title: A Molecular Dynamic Theory of Chromatography
annotation: A molecule alternating at random between moving and adsorbed phases in chromatography; the band's speed is the time-averaged velocity and its spreading comes from the fluctuations.

authors: Aris, R.
title: On the dispersion of a solute in a fluid flowing through a tube
venue: Proceedings of the Royal Society A 235(1200):67-77
annotation: Method of moments for Taylor dispersion, adding molecular diffusion and giving the effective dispersion coefficient in general geometries.

authors: Kubo, R.
title: Statistical-Mechanical Theory of Irreversible Processes. I. General Theory and Simple Applications to Magnetic and Conduction Problems
venue: Journal of the Physical Society of Japan 12(6):570-586
annotation: Linear response theory: transport coefficients as integrated correlation functions, the other half of the Green-Kubo formula.

authors: Redfield, A. G.
title: On the Theory of Relaxation Processes
venue: IBM Journal of Research and Development 1(1):19-31
annotation: Relaxation theory for spins coupled to fast fluctuations. The operators do not commute, and the rates and frequency shifts come from integrated correlations, as in the any-equation page with commutators.

authors: Blume, M.
title: Stochastic Theory of Line Shape: Generalization of the Kubo-Anderson Model
annotation: Generalizes the Kubo-Anderson stochastic line-shape model to fluctuating Hamiltonians that do not commute at different times.

authors: Szabo, A., Shoup, D., Northrup, S. H. and McCammon, J. A.
title: Stochastically gated diffusion-influenced reactions
annotation: Diffusion-influenced reactions whose reactivity is switched on and off by a stochastic gate.

authors: Zwanzig, R.
title: Rate processes with dynamical disorder
annotation: Rate processes with dynamical disorder: reaction rates that fluctuate in time, with fast and slow fluctuation limits.

authors: Jülicher, F., Ajdari, A. and Prost, J.
title: Modeling molecular motors
annotation: Molecular motors as particles switching between potentials under a chemical cycle that breaks detailed balance.

authors: Reimann, P.
title: Brownian motors: noisy transport far from equilibrium
annotation: A review of Brownian motors, where directed transport needs broken detailed balance and broken symmetry.

authors: Lawley, S. D. and Keener, J. P.
title: A New Derivation of Robin Boundary Conditions through Homogenization of a Stochastically Switching Boundary
venue: SIAM Journal on Applied Dynamical Systems 14(4):1845-1867
annotation: Derives Robin boundary conditions by homogenizing a boundary that switches at random between absorbing and reflecting.

authors: Lewontin, R. C. and Cohen, D.
title: On Population Growth in a Randomly Varying Environment
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences 62(4):1056-1060
annotation: Population growth in a randomly varying environment: the expected population and the typical population grow at different rates.

authors: Tuljapurkar, S. D.
title: Population dynamics in variable environments. II. Correlated environments, sensitivity analysis and dynamics
annotation: The small-noise formula for the stochastic growth rate of structured populations in correlated environments, including the effect of autocorrelation.

authors: Fredkin, D. R. and Rice, J. A.
title: On aggregated Markov processes
annotation: Aggregated Markov processes, as used for ion channels observed only as open or closed, and what can be identified from them.

authors: Othmer, H. G., Dunbar, S. R. and Alt, W.
title: Models of dispersal in biological systems
annotation: Velocity-jump models of dispersal, with the diffusion limit given by the integrated velocity correlation.

authors: Tuljapurkar, S.
title: Population Dynamics in Variable Environments
annotation: A monograph on population dynamics in variable environments, with products of random matrices and small-noise expansions.

authors: Schnitzer, M. J.
title: Theory of continuum random walks and application to chemotaxis
annotation: Continuum random walks with run-and-tumble motion and their effective diffusion and drift in chemotaxis.

authors: Peccoud, J. and Ycart, B.
title: Markovian Modeling of Gene-Product Synthesis
annotation: The telegraph model of gene expression: a promoter switching between two states modulates the rate of synthesis.

authors: Paulsson, J.
title: Summing up the noise in gene networks
annotation: Decomposes noise in gene networks into contributions whose size depends on the time-averaging of fluctuating upstream signals.

authors: Kussell, E. and Leibler, S.
title: Phenotypic Diversity, Population Growth, and Information in Fluctuating Environments
annotation: Phenotype switching in a fluctuating environment, relating long-run population growth to the information the population has about the environment.

authors: Raj, A., Peskin, C. S., Tranchina, D., Vargas, D. Y. and Tyagi, S.
title: Stochastic mRNA Synthesis in Mammalian Cells
annotation: Single-molecule counts showing transcriptional bursting in mammalian cells, fitted by a switching promoter model.

authors: Bressloff, P. C.
title: Stochastic switching in biology: from genotype to phenotype
annotation: A review of stochastic switching in biology, from gene expression and ion channels to motors and switching environments, with quasi-steady-state and averaging methods.

authors: He, Q.-M. and Neuts, M. F.
title: Markov chains with marked transitions
annotation: Markov chains with marked transitions, a general framework for arrival processes driven by a hidden chain.

authors: Asmussen, S.
title: Applied Probability and Queues
venue: Springer, Stochastic Modelling and Applied Probability 51, 2nd ed.
annotation: Applied probability and queues, including Markov-modulated arrivals and their asymptotic variance.

authors: Dean, J. and Barroso, L. A.
title: The tail at scale
annotation: Tail latency in large distributed systems and hedged requests, where the first of several responses wins.

authors: Benveniste, A., Métivier, M. and Priouret, P.
title: Adaptive Algorithms and Stochastic Approximations
annotation: Adaptive algorithms driven by Markovian data, analysed by averaging to an ordinary differential equation and by fluctuation limits.

authors: Duchi, J. C., Agarwal, A., Johansson, M. and Jordan, M. I.
title: Ergodic Mirror Descent
annotation: Stochastic mirror descent with data from an ergodic process, with convergence rates depending on the mixing time.

authors: Gürbüzbalaban, M., Ozdaglar, A. and Parrilo, P. A.
title: Why random reshuffling beats stochastic gradient descent
annotation: Shows that sampling without replacement (random reshuffling) beats independent sampling, so the order in which data is visited matters.

authors: Cox, D. R.
title: Some Statistical Methods Connected with Series of Events
venue: Journal of the Royal Statistical Society B 17(2):129-164
annotation: Series of events, introducing the doubly stochastic Poisson process now called the Cox process.

authors: Marley, A. A. J. and Colonius, H.
title: The “horse race” random utility model for choice probabilities and reaction times, and its competing risks interpretation
annotation: The horse-race random utility model for choices and response times, and its reading as competing risks.

authors: Taylor, G. I.
title: Diffusion by Continuous Movements
venue: Proceedings of the London Mathematical Society s2-20(1):196-212
annotation: Shows that a particle carried by a turbulent velocity spreads, at long times, with a diffusivity equal to the time integral of the velocity autocorrelation. This is the first Green-Kubo formula.

authors: Kraichnan, R. H.
title: Small-Scale Structure of a Scalar Field Convected by Turbulence
annotation: A scalar advected by a random velocity that is delta-correlated in time, the model in which the eddy diffusivity is exact.

authors: Hasselmann, K.
title: Stochastic climate models Part I. Theory
annotation: Slow climate variables driven by fast weather treated as a diffusion approximation, with the fast variables entering as noise.

authors: McLaughlin, D. W., Papanicolaou, G. C. and Pironneau, O. R.
title: Convection of Microstructure and Related Problems
annotation: Homogenization of a flow with small-scale structure: the effective large-scale equations acquire an eddy term from a cell problem.

authors: Frisch, U., She, Z. S. and Sulem, P. L.
title: Large-scale flow driven by the anisotropic kinetic alpha effect
annotation: Multiscale expansion of the Navier-Stokes equations around a small-scale flow that lacks parity invariance, giving a large-scale instability at first order.

authors: Avellaneda, M. and Majda, A. J.
title: An integral representation and bounds on the effective diffusivity in passive advection by laminar and turbulent flows
annotation: An integral representation and bounds for the effective diffusivity of a passive scalar in periodic and random flows.

authors: Dubrulle, B. and Frisch, U.
title: Eddy viscosity of parity-invariant flow
annotation: Derives the eddy viscosity of the Navier-Stokes equations by multiscale expansion around a parity-invariant small-scale flow.

authors: Fannjiang, A. and Papanicolaou, G.
title: Convection Enhanced Diffusion for Periodic Flows
annotation: Effective diffusivity of a passive scalar in periodic cellular flows, and how it scales with the molecular diffusivity.

authors: Frisch, U.
title: Turbulence: The Legacy of A. N. Kolmogorov
annotation: A book on turbulence with chapters on multiscale methods, eddy viscosity and the closure problem.

authors: Majda, A. J. and Kramer, P. R.
title: Simplified models for turbulent diffusion: Theory, numerical modelling, and physical phenomena
annotation: A review of turbulent diffusion in simplified random and periodic flows, including homogenization, eddy diffusivity and anomalous regimes.

authors: Majda, A. J., Timofeyev, I. and Vanden-Eijnden, E.
title: A mathematical framework for stochastic climate models
venue: Communications on Pure and Applied Mathematics 54(8):891-974
annotation: Eliminates fast modes of fluid and climate equations by the diffusion approximation, giving reduced stochastic equations for the slow modes.

authors: Carrasco, M., Hu, L. and Ploberger, W.
title: Optimal Test for Markov Switching Parameters
annotation: An information-matrix-type test for Markov switching that uses only the model under the null and is asymptotically equivalent to the likelihood ratio test.

authors: White, H.
title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Misspecified Models
annotation: Introduces the information-matrix test, based on the difference between the two forms of the information matrix.

authors: Chesher, A.
title: Testing for Neglected Heterogeneity
annotation: Shows that the score test for random coefficients is close to the information-matrix test.

authors: Hansen, B. E.
title: The likelihood ratio test under nonstandard conditions: Testing the Markov switching model of GNP
annotation: A bound for the likelihood ratio test of Markov switching when nuisance parameters are unidentified under the null.

authors: Garcia, R.
title: Asymptotic Null Distribution of the Likelihood Ratio Test in Markov Switching Models
annotation: The asymptotic null distribution of the sup likelihood ratio test for Markov switching.

authors: Cho, J. S. and White, H.
title: Testing for Regime Switching
annotation: Quasi-likelihood ratio tests for regime switching based on mixtures.

authors: Jarque, C. M. and Bera, A. K.
title: Efficient tests for normality, homoscedasticity and serial independence of regression residuals
annotation: The skewness and kurtosis test of normality of regression residuals.

authors: Clark, P. K.
title: A Subordinated Stochastic Process Model with Finite Variance for Speculative Prices
annotation: Returns as a normal variance mixture subordinated to a random clock, with fat tails.

authors: Aït-Sahalia, Y.
title: Maximum Likelihood Estimation of Discretely Sampled Diffusions: A Closed-form Approximation Approach
annotation: Closed-form Hermite expansions of the transition densities of diffusions for maximum likelihood estimation.

authors: Margrabe, W.
title: The value of an option to exchange one asset for another
annotation: Prices the option to exchange one lognormal asset for another in closed form, using the second asset as numeraire.

authors: Carmona, R. and Durrleman, V.
title: Pricing and hedging spread options
annotation: Surveys the models and numerical methods used to price and hedge spread options.

authors: Longin, F. and Solnik, B.
title: Extreme correlation of international equity markets
annotation: Uses extreme-value theory to show that international equity correlation rises in bear markets but not in bull markets, and is tied to the market trend rather than to volatility.

authors: Ang, A. and Chen, J.
title: Asymmetric correlations of equity portfolios
annotation: Measures exceedance correlations of US stocks with the market, finds them much larger on the downside, and finds regime-switching models capture the asymmetry better than other models tried.

authors: Hong, Y. and Tu, J. and Zhou, G.
title: Asymmetries in stock returns: statistical tests and economic evaluation
annotation: Gives model-free tests for asymmetric correlations, betas and covariances, and measures their value to an investor.

authors: Fouque, J.-P. and Pun, C. S. and Wong, H. Y.
title: Portfolio optimization with ambiguous correlation and stochastic volatilities
venue: SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization 54(5), 2309-2338
annotation: Solves worst-case portfolio choice over an ambiguous correlation between two assets, with an asymptotic closed form when their volatilities are fast mean-reverting.

authors: Driessen, J. and Maenhout, P. J. and Vilkov, G.
title: The price of correlation risk: evidence from equity options
annotation: Finds that market-wide correlation risk is priced, from S&P 100 index options against options on its components.

authors: Buraschi, A. and Porchia, P. and Trojani, F.
title: Correlation risk and optimal portfolio choice
annotation: Solves intertemporal portfolio choice with a stochastic (Wishart) covariance matrix and finds a distinct hedging demand against correlation risk.

authors: Bru, M.-F.
title: Wishart processes
annotation: Introduces the Wishart process, a matrix-valued diffusion later used to model stochastic covariance.

authors: Da Fonseca, J. and Grasselli, M. and Tebaldi, C.
title: Option pricing when correlations are stochastic: an analytical framework
annotation: An analytical framework for option pricing with stochastic correlation, built on Wishart covariance dynamics.

authors: Gourieroux, C. and Sufana, R.
title: Derivative pricing with Wishart multivariate stochastic volatility
venue: Journal of Business and Economic Statistics 28(3), 438-451
annotation: Prices derivatives when the covariance matrix of several assets follows a Wishart process.

authors: Deelstra, G. and Simon, M.
title: Multivariate European option pricing in a Markov-modulated Levy framework
venue: Journal of Computational and Applied Mathematics 317, 171-187
annotation: Prices multi-asset European options when the parameters of a Levy model are modulated by a Markov chain.

authors: Merton, R. C.
title: Lifetime Portfolio Selection under Uncertainty: The Continuous-Time Case
venue: The Review of Economics and Statistics 51(3), 247-257
annotation: Solves continuous-time consumption and investment with constant parameters, giving the constant-proportion rule for CRRA utility.

authors: Merton, R. C.
title: Optimum consumption and portfolio rules in a continuous-time model
annotation: Extends the continuous-time portfolio problem to general utilities and changing investment opportunities.

authors: Zhou, X. Y. and Li, D.
title: Continuous-Time Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection: A Stochastic LQ Framework
annotation: Solves the continuous-time Markowitz problem by stochastic linear-quadratic control and gives the efficient frontier in closed form.

authors: Zhou, X. Y. and Yin, G.
title: Markowitz's Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection with Regime Switching: A Continuous-Time Model
venue: SIAM Journal on Control and Optimization 42(4), 1466-1482
annotation: Solves the continuous-time Markowitz problem when the rate, drifts and volatilities follow an observed Markov chain, with the frontier given by two systems of linear equations.

authors: Yin, G. and Zhou, X. Y.
title: Markowitz's Mean-Variance Portfolio Selection With Regime Switching: From Discrete-Time Models to Their Continuous-Time Limits
annotation: Aggregates a large fast chain into a switching-diffusion limit, restates the continuous-time frontier and shows that strategies built from the limit are asymptotically optimal.

authors: Bäuerle, N. and Rieder, U.
title: Portfolio Optimization With Markov-Modulated Stock Prices and Interest Rates
annotation: Solves utility maximization of terminal wealth with rate, drift and volatility modulated by an observed chain, and compares it with a market of averaged data.

authors: Sotomayor, L. R. and Cadenillas, A.
title: Explicit Solutions of Consumption-Investment Problems in Financial Markets with Regime Switching
annotation: Gives explicit consumption and investment rules for HARA utilities when market parameters follow an observed regime.

authors: Zhang, Q. and Yin, G.
title: Nearly-Optimal Asset Allocation in Hybrid Stock Investment Models
venue: Journal of Optimization Theory and Applications 121(2), 419-444
annotation: Aggregates the classes of a fast, large Markov chain in a stock investment model and builds nearly optimal allocations from the limit problem.

authors: Yang, Z. and Yin, G. and Wang, L. Y. and Zhang, H.
title: Near-optimal mean-variance controls under two-time-scale formulations and applications
annotation: Derives a limit mean-variance problem as a fast chain is aggregated and shows that controls built from it are nearly optimal.

authors: Rieder, U. and Bäuerle, N.
title: Portfolio optimization with unobservable Markov-modulated drift process
annotation: Reduces portfolio choice with a hidden Markov-modulated drift to a fully observed problem by filtering and solves it for log and power utility.

authors: Sass, J. and Haussmann, U. G.
title: Optimizing the terminal wealth under partial information: The drift process as a continuous time Markov chain
annotation: Finds optimal portfolios when the drift is a hidden continuous-time Markov chain filtered from observed prices.

authors: Honda, T.
title: Optimal portfolio choice for unobservable and regime-switching mean returns
venue: Journal of Economic Dynamics and Control 28(1), 45-78
annotation: Studies portfolio choice when mean returns switch between regimes that the investor must infer from prices.

authors: Wonham, W. M.
title: Some Applications of Stochastic Differential Equations to Optimal Nonlinear Filtering
venue: Journal of the Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics, Series A: Control 2(3), 347-369
annotation: Derives the filter for a finite-state Markov chain observed through a diffusion, the basis of regime learning from prices.

authors: Tu, J.
title: Is Regime Switching in Stock Returns Important in Portfolio Decisions?
annotation: Finds certainty-equivalent losses above two percent a year from ignoring regime switching in stock returns.

authors: Kramer, M. and Lyne, A. G. and O'Brien, J. T. and Jordan, C. A. and Lorimer, D. R.
title: A Periodically Active Pulsar Giving Insight into Magnetospheric Physics
annotation: Shows that PSR B1931+24 switches its radio emission on for 5 to 10 days and off for 25 to 35 days, and spins down about 50% faster when on.

authors: Lyne, A. and Hobbs, G. and Kramer, M. and Stairs, I. and Stappers, B.
title: Switched Magnetospheric Regulation of Pulsar Spin-Down
annotation: Shows that timing noise in many pulsars comes from abrupt, often quasi-periodic switching between two spin-down rates, correlated with changes in pulse shape.

authors: Boynton, P. E. and Groth, E. J. and Hutchinson, D. P. and Nanos, G. P. and Partridge, R. B. and Wilkinson, D. T.
title: Optical Timing of the Crab Pulsar, NP 0532
annotation: Models the timing noise of the Crab pulsar as random walks in phase, frequency or spin-down rate and finds a random walk in frequency.

authors: Cordes, J. M. and Helfand, D. J.
title: Pulsar timing. III - Timing noise of 50 pulsars
annotation: Characterizes the timing noise of 50 pulsars in terms of random walks in phase, frequency and spin-down rate.

authors: Hobbs, G. and Lyne, A. G. and Kramer, M.
title: An analysis of the timing irregularities for 366 pulsars
venue: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society 402(2):1027-1048
annotation: Analyses the long-term timing irregularities of 366 pulsars observed at Jodrell Bank.

authors: van Haasteren, R. and Levin, Y.
title: Understanding and analysing time-correlated stochastic signals in pulsar timing
venue: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society 428(2):1147-1159
annotation: Treats red timing noise as a Gaussian process and shows how to analyse it together with the timing-model fit.

authors: Levermore, C. D. and Pomraning, G. C. and Sanzo, D. L. and Wong, J.
title: Linear transport theory in a random medium
annotation: Derives a formally exact equation for transport through a purely absorbing random mixture and solves it for two materials with Markov statistics, giving the two-exponential transmission law.

authors: Levermore, C. D. and Wong, J. and Pomraning, G. C.
title: Renewal theory for transport processes in binary statistical mixtures
annotation: Treats purely absorbing binary mixtures with arbitrary chord-length distributions by renewal theory and obtains effective cross sections and sources for a standard transport equation.

authors: Malvagi, F. and Levermore, C. D. and Pomraning, G. C.
title: Asymptotic limits of a statistical transport description
annotation: Studies limits of the two-equation stochastic transport model, including fluid packets small compared with the mean free path, where the model reduces to a single transport equation.

authors: Pomraning, G. C.
title: Linear Kinetic Theory and Particle Transport in Stochastic Mixtures
annotation: The monograph on particle transport through random mixtures of immiscible materials, including the Levermore-Pomraning model.

authors: Su, B. and Pomraning, G. C.
title: Limiting correlation length solutions in stochastic radiative transfer
venue: Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer 51, 893-912
annotation: Constructs solutions of stochastic radiative transfer in the limits of small and large correlation length, with scattering, in rod geometry.

authors: Pomraning, G. C.
title: Small correlation length solutions for planar symmetry beam transport in a stochastic medium
annotation: Gives small-correlation-length solutions for beam transport through a planar stochastic medium.

authors: Kiedrowski, B. C. and Vu, E. H.
title: Transit-Length Distribution for Particle Transport in Binary Markovian Mixed Media
annotation: Maps transport in a binary Markovian mixture to the telegraph process and derives the distribution of distance travelled in each material, with a Gaussian form for well-mixed media.

authors: Adams, M. L. and Larsen, E. W. and Pomraning, G. C.
title: Benchmark results for particle transport in a binary Markov statistical medium
venue: Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer 42, 253-266
annotation: Sets out the standard planar benchmark problems for transport in binary Markovian mixtures.

authors: Brantley, P. S.
title: A benchmark comparison of Monte Carlo particle transport algorithms for binary stochastic mixtures
venue: Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer 112, 599-618
annotation: Compares Monte Carlo algorithms, including chord-length sampling, on the binary-mixture benchmark suite.

authors: Larmier, C. and Hugot, F.-X. and Malvagi, F. and Mazzolo, A. and Zoia, A.
title: Benchmark solutions for transport in d-dimensional Markov binary mixtures
venue: Journal of Quantitative Spectroscopy and Radiative Transfer 189, 133-148
annotation: Computes benchmark solutions for transport through binary mixtures generated as coloured Poisson tessellations in one, two and three dimensions.

authors: Titov, G. A.
title: Statistical Description of Radiation Transfer in Clouds
annotation: Describes radiation transfer in broken cloud fields modelled with Poisson point processes whose inputs are cloud fraction and mean cloud size.

authors: Malvagi, F. and Byrne, R. N. and Pomraning, G. C. and Somerville, R. C. J.
title: Stochastic Radiative Transfer in Partially Cloudy Atmosphere
annotation: Shows that Titov's integral Markovian cloud model is a special case of a low-order differential model of the Levermore-Pomraning type and recommends the latter for climate models.

authors: Natta, A. and Panagia, N.
title: Extinction in inhomogeneous clouds
annotation: Derives analytic expressions for the extinction produced by clumpy dust layers.

authors: Hobson, M. P. and Scheuer, P. A. G.
title: Radiative transfer in a clumpy medium - I. Analytical Markov-process solution for an N-phase slab
venue: Monthly Notices of the Royal Astronomical Society 264, 145-160
annotation: Solves radiative transfer through a slab whose material along a ray is an N-phase Markov process, with absorption and isotropic scattering.

authors: Kostinski, A. B.
title: On the extinction of radiation by a homogeneous but spatially correlated random medium
venue: Journal of the Optical Society of America A 18, 1929
annotation: Shows that a statistically homogeneous but spatially correlated medium attenuates radiation more slowly than the exponential law.

authors: Vasques, R. and Larsen, E. W.
title: Non-classical particle transport with angular-dependent path-length distributions. II: Application to pebble bed reactor cores
annotation: Applies transport with non-exponential, direction-dependent path-length distributions to pebble-bed reactor cores.

authors: Smith, W. L. and Wilkinson, W. E.
title: On Branching Processes in Random Environments
annotation: Shows that a Galton-Watson process in an i.i.d. random environment dies out with probability one exactly when the expected log of the mean offspring number is not positive.

authors: Athreya, K. B. and Karlin, S.
title: On Branching Processes with Random Environments: I: Extinction Probabilities
annotation: Extends the extinction criterion for branching processes to stationary ergodic environments, where the sign of the typical log growth decides extinction.

authors: Arnold, L.
title: A Formula Connecting Sample and Moment Stability of Linear Stochastic Systems
annotation: Relates the growth rates of the moments of a linear stochastic system to its almost-sure Lyapunov exponent through the convex moment Lyapunov function.

authors: Wong, E. and Zakai, M.
title: On the Convergence of Ordinary Integrals to Stochastic Integrals
annotation: Shows that ordinary differential equations driven by smooth approximations of Brownian motion converge to the Stratonovich stochastic differential equation.

authors: Wang, W. and Zhao, X.-Q.
title: Threshold Dynamics for Compartmental Epidemic Models in Periodic Environments
venue: Journal of Dynamics and Differential Equations 20, 699-717
annotation: Defines the basic reproduction number for compartmental epidemic models with periodic coefficients and proves that it is the invasion threshold.

authors: Gray, A. and Greenhalgh, D. and Hu, L. and Mao, X. and Pan, J.
title: A Stochastic Differential Equation SIS Epidemic Model
annotation: Perturbs the transmission rate of the SIS model by white noise and shows that the almost-sure extinction threshold falls below the deterministic reproduction number.

authors: Gray, A. and Greenhalgh, D. and Mao, X. and Pan, J.
title: The SIS epidemic model with Markovian switching
venue: Journal of Mathematical Analysis and Applications 394, 496-516
annotation: Switches the rates of the SIS model by a finite Markov chain and shows that almost-sure extinction or persistence is decided by the stationary average of the per-capita growth rate, not by the reproduction number of the mean system.

authors: Hernandez-Suarez, C. and Rabinovich, J. and Hernandez, K.
title: The long-run distribution of births across environments under environmental stochasticity and its use in the calculation of unconditional life-history parameters
annotation: Computes life-history parameters averaged over a Markovian environment, including a reproduction parameter that governs growth of the expected population.

authors: Bacaër, N. and Khaladi, M.
title: On the basic reproduction number in a random environment
annotation: Defines a reproduction number for populations in a Markovian random environment whose position relative to one decides growth or decay of typical populations, and contrasts it with a parameter for the expected population.

authors: Benaïm, M. and Le Borgne, S. and Malrieu, F. and Zitt, P.-A.
title: On the stability of planar randomly switched systems
annotation: Shows that random switching between two stable planar linear systems can produce an unstable system, depending on the switching rate.

authors: Li, D. and Liu, S. and Cui, J.
title: Threshold dynamics and ergodicity of an SIRS epidemic model with Markovian switching
annotation: Gives the extinction and persistence threshold of an SIRS model whose rates switch with a Markov chain, as a stationary average over regimes.

authors: Prodhomme, A. and Strickler, É.
title: Large population asymptotics for a multitype stochastic SIS epidemic model in randomly switching environment
annotation: Studies a multitype stochastic SIS epidemic in a switching environment and shows that the sign of the top Lyapunov exponent of the linearized switched system governs the time to extinction.

authors: Monmarché, P. and Strickler, É.
title: Asymptotic expansion of the invariant measure for Markov-modulated ODEs at high frequency
annotation: Expands the invariant measure of ordinary differential equations modulated by a fast Markov chain in powers of the switching time, with a first-order formula for the top Lyapunov exponent of switched linear systems.

authors: Monmarché, P. and Schreiber, S. J. and Strickler, É.
title: Impacts of Tempo and Mode of Environmental Fluctuations on Population Growth: Slow- and Fast-Limit Approximations of Lyapunov Exponents for Periodic and Random Environments
annotation: Gives first-order slow- and fast-switching approximations of the Lyapunov exponent of structured populations switched periodically or by a Markov chain, the closest prior work to the almost-sure formula here.
